title: Northwestern vs UIUC: control, tuition, size
summary: Northwestern University (Northwestern) versus University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC). Also searched as UIUC vs Northwestern. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Northwestern University and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Northwestern vs UIUC) differ significantly in ownership, size, cost, and location. Northwestern University is a private nonprofit institution located in Evanston, while UIUC is a public university based in Champaign. The undergraduate enrollment at Northwestern is 9,201 students, considerably smaller than UIUC's 36,258 undergraduates. Tuition costs also vary greatly, with Northwestern charging $68,322 for in-state students compared to UIUC's $16,004. These distinctions highlight the differences in institutional structure and scale between Northwestern vs UIUC.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance between Northwestern University and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Northwestern vs UIUC), there are notable differences. Northwestern University, as a private institution, charges $68,322 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition. In contrast, UIUC, a public university, has a tuition of $16,004 for in-state students and $35,124 for out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who completed their programs at Northwestern is $15,000, while at UIUC, it is slightly higher at $19,500. These figures illustrate the financial considerations prospective students face when choosing between Northwestern vs UIUC.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Northwestern University and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Northwestern vs UIUC) offer distinct learning environments shaped by their campus settings and student populations. Northwestern, located in Evanston, Illinois, has an undergraduate enrollment of 9,201 students, fostering a smaller campus community. In contrast, UIUC, situated in Champaign, Illinois, serves a much larger undergraduate body of 36,258 students. These differences in size and location contribute to varied campus experiences and learning models between Northwestern vs UIUC.

sections.heading: Pick Northwestern if
paragraphs: Pick Northwestern University if you prefer a private nonprofit institution with a highly selective admission rate of approximately 7.7%. Northwestern offers a more intimate undergraduate experience with a smaller student body compared to public universities. The tuition for Northwestern is $68,322 for all students, reflecting its private status. Additionally, Northwestern boasts a strong completion rate, with about 95.1% of students finishing their programs within 150% of the expected time. These factors make Northwestern a suitable choice for students seeking a rigorous academic environment with a high likelihood of degree completion.

sections.heading: Pick UIUC if
paragraphs: Pick the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (UIUC) if you are looking for a public university with a more accessible admission rate of about 42.37%. UIUC offers significantly lower tuition for in-state students at $16,004, making it a cost-effective option compared to private institutions. The university also has a strong completion rate, with approximately 85.13% of students finishing their degrees within 150% of the expected time. These factors make UIUC an attractive choice for students seeking affordability and a solid likelihood of degree completion.
